definitions.explanation: Unable to wait calmly; tending to rush or hurry. Describes someone who wants things done quickly and gets frustrated by delays.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はせっかちで、エレベーターを{待|ま}てずに{階段|かいだん}を{使|つか}う。
examples.english: He's impatient and takes the stairs because he can't wait for the elevator.

examples.japanese: せっかちな{性格|せいかく}を{直|なお}したい。
examples.english: I want to fix my impatient nature.

examples.japanese: そんなにせっかちにならないで。まだ{時間|じかん}はある。
examples.english: Don't be so impatient. We still have time.

notes:
USAGE:
・せっかちな{人|ひと}/{性格|せいかく} (an impatient person/personality)
・せっかちになる (to become impatient)

NUANCE:
Generally mildly negative, suggesting someone who rushes unnecessarily or can't relax. Often used self-deprecatingly.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・せっかちを{起|お}こす (to get impatient - somewhat literary)
・せっかちな{食|た}べ{方|かた} (eating quickly/hastily)

ETYMOLOGY:
From the verb {急|せ}く (to hurry) plus the suffix ～かち (tendency toward). Literally "tendency to rush."

CONTRAST:
・せっかち ↔ のんびり (impatient ↔ easygoing/relaxed)
・せっかち ↔ {気長|きなが} (impatient ↔ patient)
